reviews.author: Brent Marchant
reviews.content: While in our youth, as we struggled to understand the puzzling nature of life, many of us likely heard our elders say, “You’ll understand someday when you get older,” advice that we probably tucked away in good faith for future reference. But how many of us actually came upon that promised understanding when we grew into adulthood? Chances are, many of us patiently awaited the arrival of such insights only to discover that said assurance about them never panned out as hoped for. In fact, I’m willing to bet that failed expectation happened more frequently than not. And, in this sophomore feature outing from director Clint Bentley, that scenario would again seem to be the case as the film’s perpetually perplexed protagonist searches for meaning. But, considering how frequently this situation tends to occur in everyday life, for me, the key question becomes, do we really need to see a movie that depicts this kind of all-too-familiar experience, one that many of us have already gone through ourselves? This widely praised character study follows the life of Robert Grainier (Joel Edgerton), a logger who toils in the forests of the Pacific Northwest in the early 20th Century. Having been orphaned at a young age without ever knowing his parents, he’s always sought explanations for life’s mysteries, but they generally eluded him, even on into adulthood. And, in an era when the world was changing rapidly on many fronts, he longed for answers, though they never materialized, leaving him constantly wondering about his existence, particularly when he witnesses unexplained injustices, tragedies and personal setbacks. While it’s true that many of us can empathize with his circumstances, we nevertheless also can’t help but ask, “Well, who hasn’t gone through that?” (This isn’t exactly new ground.) In that sense, then, the film focuses on the yearning of a lost soul constantly striving for some grand revelation that never arrives, and it tries to elevate this notion to the level of something that’s never been conceived of before. Moreover, to emphasize the nobility of this point, the picture dresses it up with allegedly lofty voice-over observations that sound profound but that, frankly, don’t add much that’s meaningful or even interesting. The filmmaker also tries to cover these shortcomings with gorgeous cinematography and a capable lead performance by Edgerton (though, considering the admittedly less-than-demanding character of the role, that’s not exactly saying much). Perhaps the picture’s strongest (and most underrated) asset is its cast of colorful supporting players, most notably William H. Macy and Kerry Condon, though, regrettably, their screen time is somewhat limited. Given the accolades that have been generously showered on this offering, I find it disappointing that it fails to live up to the hype, both in terms of its cinematic attributes and, more importantly, the depth of its content. Maybe I’ll understand it better when I get older. But, given that there’s not much to understand in the first place, I sincerely doubt it.

reviews.author: Manuel São Bento
reviews.content:
I had high expectations going into TRAIN DREAMS, largely due to the heartwarming reception it received from friends and peers in the industry, along with some awards buzz. The film embraces 'slow cinema' at its most contemplative and dreamy, prioritizing mood and texture over a conventional plot. I'm a sucker for natural cinematography, and here the viewers are treated to pure visual cinema, capitalizing on the real wonders of our world with stunning static shots of sunsets near rivers and cabins deep in the woods. Even though the movie feels somewhat derivative and its trajectory becomes clear fairly quickly, it never drags or becomes dull thanks to the incredibly atmospheric score and the lyrical narration, which sets a poetic tone without ever feeling too heavy.

At the heart of it all is Joel Edgerton, who delivers a career-best performance. It's a fantastic example of an "underperformance", a quiet display where dialogue is sparse, yet the actor transmits a universe of emotion, grief, and resilience exclusively through his facial expressions. It's a beautifully sad yet inspiring story about life, death, and endurance, sprinkled with surprisingly amusing moments of humor throughout the runtime. While I wish the film had gone deeper into some of its themes — specifically regarding cases of severe complicity from the protagonist, as well as the rawer edges of his grief — I understand that doing so might have worked against the dialogue-light structure Clint Bentley aimed for.

TRAIN DREAMS ultimately stands as a testament to the power of enduring, proving that a quiet life is just as worthy of witnessing as a loud one.

Rating: B

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In early 20th-century America, day laborer Robert Grainier experiences love, devastating loss, and the profound passage of time as the rapid expansion of modern industrialization reshapes the Pacific Northwest.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Set against the majestic backdrop of the Pacific Northwest in the early 1900s, Robert Grainier builds a simple life as a logger and railroad worker while starting a family with his beloved wife, Gladys. While away at work to support his family, a catastrophic wildfire sweeps through his valley, tragically destroying his home and leaving his wife and daughter missing. Overwhelmed by grief, Robert rebuilds his cabin in solitude and learns to navigate the quiet aches of memory amidst a rapidly modernizing world. Through decades of physical labor, solitary reflection, and fleeting encounters, he finds a subtle, enduring connection to the changing wilderness around him.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Orphaned at a young age, Robert Grainier grows into adulthood in the lush forests of the Pacific Northwest, securing work in logging and railroad construction during the dawn of the 20th century. He marries Gladys Olding, and together they build a modest log cabin along the Moyie River to raise their young daughter, Kate. To provide for his family, Robert takes on seasonal contracts that keep him away for long stretches, during which he witnesses both the brutal sacrifices of industrial labor and the casual cruelties of fellow workers. Disaster strikes when a massive wildfire engulfs the valley, obliterating his home and leaving his wife and child lost to the flames. Devastated, Robert returns to the ash-filled ruins and slowly rebuilds the cabin with his own hands as a sanctuary for his lingering grief. As the years pass, he faces the economic shifts following World War I, ultimately retiring from logging as newer machinery and younger crews make his traditional methods obsolete. He lives a solitary existence in the woods, occasionally haunted by visions of his lost family and the spirits of those he met along his journey. In his final years, Robert witnesses the dizzying pace of modern progress—from space travel broadcasts to his own thrilling ride in a biplane—before passing away peacefully in his sleep. His journey stands as a quiet tribute to an unsung life lived in harmony with nature and amidst the relentless march of time.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Based on Denis Johnson's acclaimed novella, 'Train Dreams' presents a sweeping yet intimate portrait of Robert Grainier, an ordinary laborer living in the Pacific Northwest during the first half of the 20th century. As railways push through dense forests and modern industrialization reshapes the American landscape, Robert seeks a peaceful life working as a logger and building a home with his wife and child. However, when sudden tragedy strikes, he is forced to navigate profound personal grief while isolated in the vast wilderness. Blending ethereal naturalism with a poignant meditation on memory, progress, and solitude, the film explores how one quiet soul endures the monumental transformations of a rapidly changing country.

story_structure.climax: In his later years, Grainier experiences a surreal and haunting encounter with a mysterious feral presence in the woods, forcing him to confront the ghost of his past and his place in nature.
story_structure.conflict: Rapid industrialization transforms the wilderness around him, bringing personal tragedy and deep existential grief when a devastating forest fire forever alters his life and surroundings.
story_structure.resolution: Grainier lives out his final days in quiet seclusion, observing a bizarre traveling wolf-boy performance that brings a strange, reflective sense of closure to a life shaped by the passage of time.
story_structure.introduction: Robert Grainier, a day laborer and logger in the American West, settles into a modest life, marries his love Gladys, and builds a cabin in the Idaho panhandle during the early 20th century.
story_structure.risingAction: Grainier navigates decades of solitary labor on the expansion of the railways, grappling with loss, encounters with local legends, and the shifting landscape of a modernizing nation.

faq.answer: Train Dreams is based on the 2011 novella of the same name written by Denis Johnson. While the main character is fictional, the setting and historic atmosphere accurately portray early 20th-century Pacific Northwest labor history.
faq.question: Is Train Dreams based on a book or a true story?

faq.answer: The film features Joel Edgerton as Robert Grainier, alongside Felicity Jones, William H. Macy, Kerry Condon, and Clifton Collins Jr.
faq.question: Who stars in Train Dreams?

faq.answer: The movie was directed by Clint Bentley, who also co-wrote the screenplay adaptation alongside Greg Kwedar.
faq.question: Who directed Train Dreams?

faq.answer: The story follows Robert Grainier, a logger and railroad builder in the Pacific Northwest, through decades of personal devotion, tragedy, and isolation as the American frontier transforms into a modern industrial society.
faq.question: What is the story of Train Dreams about?

faq.answer: While set in the American West, it is considered a post-Western or frontier drama, focusing on the quiet, contemplative life of a working-class logger rather than traditional gunfights or cowboy tropes.
